summary: The study describes the successful development of plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) of tantalum nitride (Ta-N) thin films using hydrogen radicals as a reducing agent. The PEALD process yielded high-density, polycrystalline Ta-N films with excellent electrical resistivity and no aging effect under air exposure. The films were deposited at 260°C using TBTDET as a precursor and hydrogen plasma for reduction.
evidence: Plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition ~PEALD! of tantalum nitride ~Ta-N! thin ﬁlms at a deposition temperature of 260°C using hydrogen radicals as a reducing agent for tertbutylimidotris ~diethylamido!tantalum is described. The PEALD yielded superior Ta-N ﬁlms with an electric resistivity of 400 mV cm and no aging effect under exposure to air. The ﬁlm density was higher than that of Ta-N ﬁlms formed by typical ALD, in which NH 3 is used instead of hydrogen radicals. In addition, the as-deposited ﬁlms were not amorphous, but rather polycrystalline structures of cubic TaN.
